items.name: FindMatches
items.summary: An iterator over all non-overlapping matches for an infallible search.

items.name: Regex
items.summary: A regular expression that uses deterministic finite automata for fast searching.

methods.name: builder
methods.summary: Return a builder for configuring the construction of a `Regex`.

methods.name: find
methods.signature: fn find<'h, I: Into<Input<'h>>>(&self, input: I) -> Option<Match>
methods.summary: Returns the start and end offset of the leftmost match. If no match exists, then `None` is returned.

methods.name: find_iter
methods.signature: fn find_iter<'r, 'h, I: Into<Input<'h>>>(&'r self, input: I) -> FindMatches<'r, 'h, A>
methods.summary: Returns an iterator over all non-overlapping leftmost matches in the given bytes. If no match exists, then the iterator yields no elements.

methods.name: forward
methods.summary: Return the underlying DFA responsible for forward matching.

methods.name: is_match
methods.signature: fn is_match<'h, I: Into<Input<'h>>>(&self, input: I) -> bool
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if this regex matches the given haystack.

methods.name: new
methods.summary: Parse the given regular expression using the default configuration and return the corresponding regex.

methods.name: new_many
methods.summary: Like `new`, but parses multiple patterns into a single "regex set." This similarly uses the default regex configuration.

methods.name: new_many_sparse
methods.summary: Like `new`, but parses multiple patterns into a single "regex set" using sparse DFAs. This otherwise similarly uses the default regex configuration.

methods.name: new_sparse
methods.summary: Parse the given regular expression using the default configuration, except using sparse DFAs, and return the corresponding regex.

methods.name: pattern_len
methods.summary: Returns the total number of patterns matched by this regex.

methods.name: reverse
methods.summary: Return the underlying DFA responsible for reverse matching.

methods.name: try_search
methods.summary: Returns the start and end offset of the leftmost match. If no match exists, then `None` is returned.
